hints: Remember the mass spectrometer separates by mass, so focus on the total mass of the $\text{O}_2^+$ ion, which is the sum of its two oxygen atoms.
Start pairing the isotopes, $^{16}\text{O}+^{16}\text{O}$ gives 32, $^{16}\text{O}+^{17}\text{O}$ gives 33, and keep going systematically.
Check your list for repeats, since two different pairs can add up to the same total mass and will give only one peak.
walkthrough:
**Understand what makes a peak**

Each peak for $\text{O}_2^+$ is a different m/z value. Since the charge is +1, m/z is just the total mass of the two O atoms.

$$m/z(\text{O}_2^+) = \text{mass of atom 1} + \text{mass of atom 2}$$

**List all possible pairs systematically**

Pair each isotope with itself and with the others. This gives all combinations present in the sample.

$$^{16}\text{O}^{16}\text{O} = 32, \quad ^{16}\text{O}^{17}\text{O} = 33, \quad ^{16}\text{O}^{18}\text{O} = 34$$
$$^{17}\text{O}^{17}\text{O} = 34, \quad ^{17}\text{O}^{18}\text{O} = 35, \quad ^{18}\text{O}^{18}\text{O} = 36$$

**Count distinct masses**

Notice that $^{16}\text{O}^{18}\text{O}$ and $^{17}\text{O}^{17}\text{O}$ both give mass 34, so they merge into one peak. The distinct masses are 32, 33, 34, 35 and 36.

That is 5 distinct peaks in total.

options.A: 3 counts only one peak per isotope. This forgets that $\text{O}_2^+$ contains two atoms, so mixed molecules like $^{16}\text{O}^{17}\text{O}$ create extra masses.
options.C: 6 counts every unordered pair as different, treating $^{16}\text{O}^{18}\text{O}$ (mass 34) and $^{17}\text{O}^{17}\text{O}$ (mass 34) as two peaks. They have the same m/z, so they give one peak.
options.D: 9 comes from $3 \times 3 = 9$ ordered pairs. This double counts because $^{16}\text{O}^{17}\text{O}$ is the same molecule as $^{17}\text{O}^{16}\text{O}$, and it also ignores the mass overlap at 34.
